config.title: Design Permission System

intro.title: Design Permission System
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple permission system for controlling access to different features in a Vue application. You will learn how to use Vue's reactive state and computed properties to manage user roles and permissions. The main technologies involved are Vue 3's Composition API with ref and computed, along with conditional rendering in the template. By the end, you'll have a functional UI where buttons or sections are shown or hidden based on the user's role, like 'admin' or 'user'.
intro.usecase: Permission systems are essential in any multi-user application to control access and actions based on user roles. In real-world products like admin dashboards (e.g., content management systems or SaaS platforms), permissions determine which users can view, edit, or delete data, manage settings, or access specific modules. As a Vue developer, you'll implement this pattern to conditionally render UI elements—such as buttons, menus, or entire form sections—ensuring a secure and tailored user experience. This lesson will equip you to build scalable, role-based interfaces that are common in enterprise software, e-commerce backends, and collaborative tools.

objectives: Implement a reactive permissions object using Vue's ref() API
Construct a computed property that determines user access levels
Apply conditional rendering directives to show/hide UI elements based on permissions
Configure a permission-checking method that validates user actions
Bind permission states to component data properties for dynamic updates
Manipulate permission flags through user interactions like checkboxes or buttons
Initialize a permission system with default roles and access levels

steps.title: Initialize user roles state
steps.instruction: Inside the PermissionSystem component, initialize a reactive state variable called 'userRoles' using ref. Set its initial value to an array containing at least one role object with 'id', 'name', and 'permissions' properties.
steps.hint: Use ref() to create reactive state. The initial value should be an array of objects representing different user roles.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a reactive 'userRoles' state variable initialized with role data.
successCriteria: A 'userRoles' variable is declared using ref() and initialized with an array containing at least one role object with id, name, and permissions properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using ref() to create reactive state and initializing it with an array of role objects containing id, name, and permissions properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: Inside the setup() function, use ref() to create a reactive state variable called 'userRoles' and initialize it with an array of role objects. Each role object should have id, name, and permissions properties.

steps.title: Initialize current role state
steps.instruction: Inside the setup function, create a reactive ref called 'currentRole' to store the ID of the currently selected role. Initialize it with the value 'admin'.
steps.hint: Use the ref function you imported earlier to create reactive state. The syntax is: const currentRole = ref('admin')

// Similar: reactive state for selected item
const selectedItem = ref('item1')
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a reactive currentRole state variable initialized with 'admin' that will track which role is currently selected.
successCriteria: A ref named 'currentRole' is created and initialized with the string value 'admin' inside the setup function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using the ref function and initializing currentRole with the string 'admin'.
steps.feedbackWrong: create a reactive ref called currentRole inside the setup function and initialize it with 'admin'.

steps.title: Define permission check handler
steps.instruction: Inside the setup function, define a function named 'hasPermission' that takes 'roleId' and 'permission' as parameters and returns a boolean value.
steps.hint: Create a function that checks if a given role has a specific permission. You can use a simple conditional check inside the function body.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named 'hasPermission' is defined inside the setup function, ready to be used for permission checks.
successCriteria: The 'hasPermission' function is defined with two parameters and returns a boolean value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your function is named 'hasPermission', takes two parameters, and returns a boolean value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The permission check handler isn't defined correctly. Check that you've created a function named 'hasPermission' inside the setup function.

steps.title: Define role selection handler
steps.instruction: Define a function named handleRoleSelect that takes a role parameter and updates the currentRole state with that role.
steps.hint: Create a function inside setup() that sets currentRole.value to the role parameter.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function handleRoleSelect is defined that updates currentRole when called with a role.
successCriteria: The handleRoleSelect function is defined inside setup() and updates currentRole.value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a function, but make sure it updates currentRole.value with the role parameter.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function isn't defined correctly. It should take a role parameter and set currentRole.value to that role.

steps.title: Add main container structure
steps.instruction: In the return object of your setup function, add a div container with an h1 heading that says 'Permission System'.
steps.hint: The return object should contain a template structure. Start by returning a div with an h1 inside it.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now returns a basic HTML structure with a heading.
successCriteria: The setup function returns an object with a template property containing a div with an h1 heading that displays 'Permission System'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're returning an object with a template property containing the div and h1.

steps.title: Add permission check demonstration
steps.instruction: Add a section in your component's template that demonstrates permission checking by calling hasPermission with hardcoded values and displaying the results.
steps.hint: Create a new div element with a heading and some paragraphs that show the result of hasPermission('create'), hasPermission('edit'), and hasPermission('view') for the current role.

Can view: {{ hasPermission('view') }}
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will now show a new section that demonstrates permission checking with static values, showing true/false results for create, edit, and view permissions based on the current role.
successCriteria: A new section is added with a heading 'Permission Check Demo' and three paragraphs showing the results of hasPermission('create'), hasPermission('edit'), and hasPermission('view') calls.
